verdict.summary: Arista is the Ethernet standard-bearer for AI back-end fabrics — the high-radix switching that wires together GPU clusters at hyperscalers. The investment case is exceptional on four of five axes: an intact medium-term uptrend (all EMAs still rising, despite a sharp early-June pullback toward the EMA50), five consecutive earnings beats, a fortress balance sheet with $12.3B net cash and net share buybacks StockAnalysis· Q1 2026, and a raised FY26 revenue guide near $11.5B TIKR· mai 2026. The honest caveat — and why this is now a B+, downgraded from A — is that at today's spot of $169.67, the R/R to TP1 ($183.25) has collapsed to 0.79 (just $13.58 upside vs $17.17 downside to the $152.50 stop). An A grade requires actionable R/R ≥ 1.5 at spot. The thesis is fully intact, but the price has moved past the published entry of $162.75 and the ~46x forward multiple leaves no margin for error. A pullback toward $157–160 would restore the grade.

business.overview:
Arista Networks designs high-performance Ethernet switches and routers for the largest data centers and cloud networks on earth. Its franchise is the spine of cloud and AI infrastructure: high-radix, low-latency switching built on merchant silicon and unified by EOS (Extensible Operating System), a single, programmable software stack that runs across the entire portfolio. That software moat is what keeps customers from treating the boxes as commodity hardware.

The strategic prize today is the AI back-end network — the dedicated fabric that connects thousands of GPUs into a single training cluster. Arista is pushing Ethernet (via the Ultra Ethernet Consortium and its 800G / next-gen 1.6T platforms) as the open standard against Nvidia's proprietary InfiniBand, and management raised its FY26 AI revenue target to $3.5B Seeking Alpha· mai 2026. Customer concentration is the flip side of that prize: Microsoft and Meta have each historically driven a large share of revenue, so Arista's growth is geared to a handful of hyperscaler capex budgets. The differentiator versus Cisco and the white-box crowd is the combination of merchant-silicon economics with EOS's operational consistency — a genuine moat, but one priced for perfection.

risks.riskSummary: The business risk is low — debt-free, cash-rich, dominant franchise. The investment risk is the premium multiple meeting a margin squeeze and hyperscaler concentration. At ~46x forward, the price leaves little room for a stumble.

risks.pedagogy: Arista's operations are about as clean as large-cap tech gets: net cash, no dilution, elite returns on capital. The risk that matters is paying ~46x forward earnings for a name whose growth is geared to a few hyperscalers while gross margins compress. None of that breaks the thesis — it just means the entry price and the stop carry more weight than usual. Trade it with disciplined sizing, not blind conviction.

tradeIdea.thesis: Wait for a pullback. The thesis is fully intact — Ethernet standard-bearer for AI fabrics, five straight beats, raised ~$11.5B FY26 guide funded from net cash, and a rising EMA stack. But at $169.67, the R/R to TP1 ($183.25) is just 0.79 ($13.58 upside vs $17.17 risk to the $152.50 stop). That does not meet the minimum 1.5R threshold for an actionable entry. A pullback into the $157–160 zone (near the EMA20 at $160.82) would restore the R/R to ~3.1R at TP1 from a $160 entry and make this a compelling swing entry again. Note: TP1 ($183.25) sits above the 52W high ($179.80), so the trade requires a breakout to new highs. Use $160 as the preferred entry—entries below $158 leave less than 1 ATR to the stop, making the position vulnerable to normal volatility on a 1.61-beta name. Do not chase into strength near the 52W high.
